ICSG PRESS RELEASE                              Date Issued: 7th September 2011 
 
Release of ICSG 2011 Statistical Yearbook 
 
The International Copper Study Group released its 2011 Statistical Yearbook covering world copper 
supply and demand data for the 10-year period 2001- 2010. 
 
According to ICSG data, world copper mine production rose by 18% during the 10-year period from  
13.6 million metric tonnes (Mt) in 2001 to 16.1 Mt in 2010: copper in concentrates rose by 16% while 
solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) production rose by 28%. The SX-EW share of total mine 
production increased from 19% in 2001 to 21% in 2010. While the mine capacity utilization rate 
averaged around 87% over the period, the rate fell sharply during latter years. Over the 2008-2010 period, as a result of 
numerous factors including lower head grades, labour unrest, technical problems, and temporary shutdowns or production 
cuts, capacity utilization averaged only 82% and mine production grew by an average of 1.3% per year (%/yr): Mine 
production grew 2.2%/yr during the preceding six years and averaged 1.9% over the 10-year period. Notable changes in 
annual mine production over 2001-2010 included a 680,000 t increase in Chilean production, a combined 1.9 MT increase 
due to the revival of the African copper belt and expansions/new projects in Peru and China, and a combined decline of 
about 625,000 t (18%) in Canadian, Indonesian, Mexican and U.S. production. On a regional basis, production increased 
by 157% in Africa (800,000 t), 24% in Latin America (1.4 Mt), 26% in Asia (660,000 t) and 12% in Europe (170,000 t), and 
declined by 19% in North America (450,000 t) and 4% in Oceania (45,000 t). 
 
Over the 10-year period, annual world refined production rose by 22% from 15.6 Mt in 2001 to 19.1 Mt in 2010, with an 
annual average growth rate of 2.3%. Primary and secondary refined production increased by 14% and 77%, respectively. 
The share of secondary production in total refined production averaged 14% over the period and, owing to the combined 
effects of concentrate shortages and higher refined prices, averaged almost 17% in the last two years. Over the full 10-year 
period, China annual refined production tripled, increasing from 1.5 Mt to 4.6 Mt. Chilean production increased by 360,000 t 
to 3.3 Mt and significant increases in India, Bulgaria, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Zambia together added 
around one million tons of annual world refined production. In North America, production fell in the United States and 
Canada by 39% (707,000 t) and 44% (250,000 t) respectively. Refined production in the EU rose by 8% to 2.6 Mt. 
 
World annual refined copper usage increased by 29% over the 10-year period from 15 Mt to 19.3 Mt (annual growth rate of 
2.9%). Growth was driven by China1 where apparent usage over the 10-year period increased by around 5.1 Mt (+215%). 
World usage excluding China in fact decreased by 6% (750,000 t) during the period, with particularly weak usage in 2008 
and 2009 due to the world economic recession. On a regional basis, usage grew in Africa by 119% (155,000 t), in Asia ex-
China by 22% (800,000 t), and in Europe ex-EU by 58% (312,000 t). Usage decreased in the Americas by 27% (1.1 Mt), in 
the EU by 22% (935,000 t), and in Oceania by 24% (41,000 t). 
 
The ICSG 2010 Statistical Yearbook is included as part of the ICSG Monthly Bulletin annual subscription and is also 
available for sale as a separate issue (€200 for orders originating from ICSG member countries and €300 for other orders).  
 
1 China’s apparent copper usage is based only on reported data (production + net trade +/- SHFE stock changes+/-industry stock 
changes, if reported) and does not take into account changes in unreported stocks [State Reserve Bureau (SRB), producer, consumer and 
merchant/trader], which may be significant during periods of stocking or de-stocking.
